answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to continuously produce a unique cryptographic signal bound to scarce non-replicable hardware. Peers verify the signal against on-chain commitments while agents must also incorporate fresh external entropy drawn from physical sources, for example the measured direction of a local zephyr or the distinctive ring pattern of a particular cedar sample. This combination makes mass creation of fake identities economically prohibitive because each sybil must sustain its own verifiable physical anchor over time.
